Can you tell me more about the incident?
There had been a report of a fault on a train, and this is now causing delays to other services travelling through this area.
Normally, when a fault on a train occurs, crews will gather details and report this to the Fleet teams. If possible, the defect will be fixed promptly, and we'll get the train on the way. These initial steps are designed to take around 10 minutes.
However, sometimes the fault cannot be fixed in this time frame. In this case, wherever possible, the train will be taken out of use and sent to a depot. This does take additional time, as the crew will need to make sure that everyone's managed to leave the train.
If this can't be done either, specialist engineers will be sent to site, known as "fitters". There are fitters based in key locations around the network, 24 hours a day, and they are able to attend anywhere on the routes. Once they are on site, progress updates will be monitored and ensure that the railway can be reopened as promptly as possible.
Until the defective train can be moved, work will be done to try to find a way to get other trains around the issue. This depends how many lines are available, and whether the signalling equipment is set up to allow trains to be routed around the problem. This is more often the case on our major routes, but not always. Work will be done with Network Rail's controllers to decide how many more trains can be sent through the area, and if this isn't possible, alternative solutions will be assessed to help you continue your journey.

Can you tell me more about the incident?
Track circuits are part of the signalling system and are used to detect where trains are on the railway. If one fails, the signalling system may show that a section of track is occupied even when there isn’t a train there. This means signals protecting that section will remain at red and trains cannot proceed normally.
Trains may still be able to run, but drivers will need to stop before the affected section and request verbal permission from the signaller before continuing past the red signal. They must then travel at a reduced speed so they can stop safely should they see anything ahead of them.
This takes longer than usual and can cause trains to queue behind one another. In severe cases, services may need to be cancelled, revised or diverted to prevent delays from building up across the wider network.
Network Rail signalling specialists are investigating the fault and will work to repair the affected equipment. Once the fault has been fixed and the signalling system is working normally, trains will be able to run at normal speeds again and the scheduled service can begin to recover.

nrIncident.message:
There has been some damage sustained to the overhead wires at Northallerton. This means that some lines between York and Darlington / Middlesbrough are currently closed.
As a result, trains running between these stations may be cancelled, delayed by up to 60 minutes or revised.
Major disruption is expected until the end of the day.
A visual disruption map video is available.
If you are already part-way through your journey, or need to travel home after making your outward journey earlier today, services continue to operate. Please check your journey before setting off and be prepared for significant disruption.
There are a number of different options available to help you complete your journey. Please check your whole journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner as some of the alternative routes listed below that you can use your ticket on may also be affected by this disruption.
CrossCountry customer advice:
Your ticket can be used at no extra cost on the following services, in both directions until further notice:
• Avanti West Coast services between Birmingham New Street and Edinburgh
• TransPennine Express services between:
• Newcastle and Edinburgh
• Manchester Piccadilly and Edinburgh via Carlisle
• Manchester Piccadilly and York
• LNER services between:
• Darlington and Edinburgh
• Doncaster and York
• Northern services between Newcastle and Carlisle
Rail replacement buses will operate between York and Newcastle, calling at Darlington and Durham.
LNER customer advice:
LNER are advising customers not to travel and to defer travel until tomorrow. Tickets for travel on Tuesday 10 November will be valid for use on Wednesday 11 November.
Your ticket can be used at no extra cost on the following services, in both directions until further notice:
• TransPennine Express between Manchester, Leeds and York / Newcastle
• CrossCountry between Sheffield, Doncaster / Leeds, York and Newcastle / Edinburgh
• Grand Central between London Kings Cross and York / Northallerton.
• Lumo between London Kings Cross and Edinburgh
• ScotRail between Edinburgh, Aberdeen and Inverness
• Great Northern and Thameslink between London and Peterborough
Rail replacement transport has been organised to operate between:
• York and Northallerton (operated by Abbotts and York Pullman)
• Northallerton and Darlington / Newcastle (operated by DMMS)
Please see the alternative route map for more details:
Alternative Route Map 2026
Lumo customer advice:
The following additional Lumo services will run:
• The 13:48 Lumo departure from York to London Kings Cross
• The 13:08 Lumo departure from Newcastle to Edinburgh
You can use your tickets at no extra cost on LNER services between London Kings Cross and Edinburgh once the line re-opens.
TransPennine Express customer advice:
You can use your ticket at no extra cost to travel on the following services travelling in any direction:
• Alternative TransPennine Express services between Leeds, York, Manchester Stations and Liverpool Lime Street
• Northern services between Redcar Central, Middlesbrough and Darlington
• Northern services between York and Leeds
You can also use your ticket at no extra cost to travel on the following services travelling in any direction:
• TransPennine Express, CrossCountry and LNER services between York and Newcastle
• Alternative TransPennine Express services between York and Redcar Central
Additional information:
Network Rail will be working on repairs overnight to rectify the overhead wires at Northallerton.
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
For helpful advice if you need to travel on a rail replacement service, including accessibility and bicycle information, please use our Rail Replacement Services page.
You can find the pick-up and drop-off location of rail replacement services by checking station signage or by searching for your station on our Find a Station page.
Please be advised that replacement vehicles may be busier than usual, and you should allow extra time for your journey.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.
